name: Rephael
overview: Rephael is a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Shemaiah. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, serving to establish lineage within the Levitical family. There are no additional notes or significant narrative details provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Rephael means 'G-d heals,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew components 'El' for God and 'repha' for healing. This proper name, while not given directly by God, carries a meaningful reminder of divine healing power.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Rephael is the son of Shemaiah, as noted in 1 Chronicles 26:7. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are documented for Rephael in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Rephael's significance lies in his role within the Levitical genealogies, which were vital for maintaining the priestly and temple service lines ordained by God. His identification as Shemaiah's son helps preserve the continuity of the tribe of Levi, which was set apart for sacred duties. Although not prominent in narrative events, his genealogical mention underscores the importance of faithful lineage in God's redemptive plan.
